notes:
Summary: evaluation focused on Dedicated capacity economics and SLA negotiation. Heavy emphasis on predictable throughput and <quote>no surprise</quote> tail latency. Key ask: a cost model that maps commit levels (GPUs) to unit token costs at different utilization bands.

PoC & metrics:
- PoC target: 4 H100-equivalent GPUs for 7 days (load shape: mixed chat + reranking).
- Traffic profile: 60% chat (longer context), 30% reranking (short queries), 10% embedding-like operations.
- Throughput target: 450-600 QPS peak, sustain 120k tokens/sec peak burst.
- Latency SLOs: p95 < 150ms for chat short-turns; p95 < 80ms for reranking; acceptable p99 fallback to cheaper model at >300ms.

Reserved GPU planning assumptions shared with customer spreadsheet:
- Commit tiers considered: 2, 4, 8, 16 GPUs.
- Utilization scenarios modeled: conservative (30% UTIL), expected (55% UTIL), aggressive (80% UTIL).
- Effective tokens/day assumptions (example): at 55% UTIL on 8 H100s ~ 120M tokens/day.

Unit economics (illustrative numbers used in PoC deck):
- Base infra cost (reserved) per GPU/month: $14,000 (negotiable).
- Fixed infra + network overhead per month: $1,600 per GPU-equivalent (ops/support attribution).
- Effective token capacity per GPU/month at 55% UTIL: ~360M tokens.
- Implied raw cost per token (infrastructure only) at 55% UTIL: $0.000043/token.
- With ops/support + margin to Redwood pricing tiers: negotiated customer-facing estimate range $0.00006 - $0.00010/token depending on commit and volume.
- Note: at 30% UTIL cost/token rises ~1.8x; at 80% UTIL cost/token drops ~0.7x.

SLA & negotiation points:
- Customer requested hard latency SLOs tied to financial credits; legal asked for example SLO addendum language.
- Routing policies: primary region (us-east) + failover to us-west; require predictable cross-region RTO < 3s for sessions.
- Fallbacks: automatic downgrade to a quantized model when capacity constrained (must preserve quality thresholds).

Security/compliance:
- Must support SSO (SAML), KMS key mirroring to customer HSM, audit log retention 7 years for targeted data flows, and data residency for EU segments.
- On-prem option: customer wants ability to burst to private cluster behind their VPC/NAT; need clarity on egress and observability hooks.

Quotes from stakeholders:
- CTO: "We need deterministic cost per query for Q3 budgeting — variability is the killer."
- Head of ML infra: "If we commit, we need a sizing spreadsheet that ties commit -> expected token throughput -> worst-case cost/token."

Open items / next steps:
- Redwood to produce final reserved-sizing spreadsheet with three utilization bands and per-token pricing for commit tiers 4/8/16 GPUs (owner: Raj).
- Legal to draft SLA addendum examples for latency credits (owner: Maya).
- Procurement: require breakdown of monthly fees vs one-time onboarding; schedule procurement sync week of 2026-03-22.

Stalled concerns: procurement needs clear escape clause for underutilization; infra wants explicit limits on KV cache eviction behavior across model rollouts.
